candidates.exact_span: no significant toxicity at the critical dilution
candidates.computation_change_reason: This phrase defines the toxicity compliance endpoint referenced throughout the TRE provisions; different interpretations of 'no significant toxicity' or 'critical dilution' could change which enforceable toxicity limit applies and whether reported measurements exceed it.

candidates.exact_span: Failure to identify the specific chemical compound causing toxicity test failure will normally result in a permit limit for whole effluent toxicity limits per federal regulations at 40 CFR 122.44(d)(1)(v).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether identification failure has occurred and whether this conditional trigger applies determines if whole effluent toxicity limits become enforceable numeric limits (Purpose A) and whether associated WET monitoring obligations are in effect (Purpose B).

candidates.exact_span: Quarterly testing during the TRE is a minimum monitoring requirement.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a minimum monitoring frequency obligation during an active TRE; whether quarterly TRE testing was required depends on whether a TRE was in effect for the evaluated period.

candidates.exact_span: Any results and interpretation of any chemical specific analysis, and for any characterization, identification, and confirmation tests performed during the quarter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines quarterly chemical-specific analysis and characterization/identification/confirmation testing as reportable TRE activities; interpretation of whether these tests were required during TRE affects monitoring-obligation applicability (B) and how missing or absent quarterly results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: A TRE may be stopped if there is no toxicity at the critical dilution for a period of 12 consecutive months (with at least monthly testing) following confirmation of toxicity in the retests.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets conditions under which TRE-related monitoring obligations may cease, including a monthly testing requirement during the 12-month period; different interpretations of whether toxicity was absent, whether monthly testing occurred, or whether retest confirmation occurred could change whether TRE monitoring was still required or whether absence of data reflects a documented no-obligation state.

candidates.exact_span: no more than a 449 mg/l net increase over the drinking water concentration
candidates.computation_change_reason: States an enforceable numeric effluent limit for total dissolved solids expressed relative to drinking water concentration; the applicable numeric limit for comparison depends on how 'net increase' and the baseline 'drinking water concentration' are interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington shall maintain the formulated two-part best management practice
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes an ongoing BMP maintenance obligation tied to the salinity control program; interpretation of what the two-part BMP requires (including any embedded monitoring) affects which monitoring obligations were applicable and how missing salinity-related evidence is classified.

candidates.exact_span: EPA recommends that permittees required to perform a TRE not rely on quarterly testing alone to ensure success in the TRE, and that additional screening tests be performed to capture toxic samples for identification of toxicants.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Distinguishes a mandatory minimum (quarterly testing) from recommended additional screening tests; interpretation of whether 'recommends' creates any enforceable monitoring obligation affects monitoring-applicability determinations and whether missing screening-test evidence indicates a gap or a non-required activity.
